title: Specify whether interacting with a numeric <input> via arrow buttons focuses it

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
Currently, the specification intentionally does not describe any sort of interface for `<input type="number">`:

> This specification does not define what user interface user agents are to use; user agent vendors are encouraged to consider what would best serve their users' needs. For example, a user agent in Persian or Arabic markets might support Persian and Arabic numeric input (converting it to the format required for submission as described above). Similarly, a user agent designed for Romans might display the value in Roman numerals rather than in decimal; or (more realistically) a user agent designed for the French market might display the value with apostrophes between thousands and commas before the decimals, and allow the user to enter a value in that manner, internally converting it to the submission format described above.

With that being said, all (desktop) browsers I'm aware of implement a "spinbox" interface--the number is displayed in a field, with up and down arrow buttons also inside the field, right-aligned:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25993062/107764928-f9995280-6cfe-11eb-8115-da7a958c56fe.png)

There's currently a difference between browsers regarding whether clicking on said arrow buttons focuses the input: Firefox does not focus the input, whereas Chromium and WebKit (via the Midori browser) do (all testing done on Linux). This has [broken at least one UI control](https://github.com/LLK/scratch-paint/issues/1111) that depends on the Chromium/WebKit behavior of focusing the input when the arrow buttons are clicked, and it's conceivable that this could break other code that expects a `focus` event to be fired whenever a numeric input is changed.

Is this worth specifying and making consistent across browsers?
